ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of each gérant, every shareholder above the 25% UBO threshold, and all indirect beneficial owners against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EC) No 2580/2001 and Regulation (EU) No 269/2014); (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, required for USD-denominated settlements and correspondent banking relationships; (iv) French national freezing measures issued by the Direction générale du Trésor under Article L.562-2 CMF; and (v) the French TRACFIN guidance under the 4AMLD/5AMLD framework. PEP screening uses a tiered model (domestic/international PEP, family members, and close associates) under Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 CMF; any PEP match triggers automatic enhanced due diligence, and the PEP risk tail applies for 12 months after cessation of public functions. Continuous transaction filtering against UN/EU/OFAC and French lists is maintained for the life of the entity; any suspicion is escalated to the compliance officer and reported to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (INPI) at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; availability verified against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), the RCS databases of the greffes des tribunaux de commerce (via infogreffe.fr), and the INPI trademark register (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin script and declared in French for RCS/RNE filing; non-French names are transliterated into the Latin alphabet and may be supplemented by a French operative or descriptive element. The name must be distinctive, lawful, not contrary to ordre public or bonnes mœurs, and must not be misleading as to the activity, size or state sponsorship. For an online retailer of 3D printers and consumables, the name must avoid likelihood of confusion with prior RNE/RCS names and prior trademarks, particularly in Nice Classes 7, 9, 35 and 42. The SARL name must appear with the legal form 'SARL' and the share capital in all deeds and correspondence.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (where use implies official state sponsorship)
Union européenne (where use implies official EU status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France maintains no statutory name-reservation ledger separate from the formation filing; the 30-day window reflects the standard validity of the professional pre-clearance search certificate (RNE/RCS/INPI database search), within which the SARL formation dossier must be filed at the guichet unique. Where the INPI/RNE rejects or suspends the dénomination sociale, the notification sets out the statutory grounds (typically confusion with an earlier RCS/RNE name, a prior trademark, or an ordre public objection). The applicant may: (a) cure and resubmit the corrected dossier within 30 days of notification without a further greffe tariff for the corrected name; (b) obtain a written coexistence/consent letter from the prior-rights holder and resubmit; (c) if the refusal persists, file an administrative appeal within 2 months of notification before the Tribunal Judiciaire competent for the INPI/RNE decision, under the general administrative-litigation rules applicable to guichet unique decisions; and (d) in parallel, apply for interim injunctive relief (référé) before the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire where the refusal causes imminent economic harm. Legal counsel should also verify unregistered marks and matching domain names before filing to minimize rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through an approved professional domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation agréée under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code) or at the gérant's tax residence with a declared right of use; the registered office must be a physical French address equipped to receive official notifications and to hold statutory records. A purely digital virtual office without physical reception, mail-handling capacity, and retention of statutory registers is not compliant; for low-risk online retail of 3D printers and consumables, a licensed domiciliation service with commercial reception and secretarial services is the accepted market practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection estimated below 5% for a low-risk online retailer of 3D printers and resin filaments, absent VAT irregularities, TRACFIN filings, adverse sanctions hits, or PEP/key-objectionable ownership flags; however, on-site verification is systemically triggered where the entity applies for a French Intra-Community VAT number, seeks CNIL/ANSSI-related registrations, or uses a domiciliation address associated with multiple shell-like entities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the impots.gouv.fr professional portal. The Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (INSEE) assigns the SIREN after company formation; the SIE assigns or confirms the French VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Form the SARL through the formalities portal operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), which transmits the registration data to the relevant authorities. INSEE assigns a SIREN and establishment-level SIRET. Register the company with the competent SIE and request a VAT number before making transactions for which VAT registration is required; the number is generally FR plus a two-digit key and the SIREN. A foreign company without a French establishment must apply to the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for VAT registration when required. A non-EU-established applicant may be required to appoint a French fiscal representative, subject to applicable statutory exceptions and mutual-assistance arrangements. Obtain an EORI number separately from customs when required for customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). An eligible SARL may elect the temporary partnership-taxation regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for up to five fiscal years, if statutory conditions are met. A qualifying family SARL may elect income-tax treatment under Article 239 bis AA, subject to continuing eligibility. France has no US-style check-the-box election. Hybrid-mismatch rules apply under French law and EU implementation; they do not provide a general classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for domestic supplies of goods under the French small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base), subject to statutory rules and applicable current-year thresholds; EUR 37,500 applies to services. These are exemption thresholds, not a general VAT-registration safe harbor. A business may opt for VAT, and a non-established taxable person making taxable supplies in France generally must register from the first relevant transaction. Cross-border distance sales and EU-wide small-business rules have separate conditions and thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is not generally a real-time invoice-clearance jurisdiction. Domestic B2B e-invoicing and transaction/payment e-reporting are being phased in: all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance begins on that date for large and intermediate-sized companies and on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope invoices must use the prescribed formats and transmission channels through an approved private platform (plateforme agréée); the DGFiP public portal provides directory and data functions. Consumer and cross-border transactions are generally subject to e-reporting rather than domestic B2B e-invoicing. No general digital tax-stamping or pre-clearance requirement applies to ordinary retail invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be exempt with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory export conditions are met and the seller can substantiate that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies are exempt with right to deduct only where the applicable conditions, including customer VAT status, transport evidence, and reporting, are satisfied. Services are not automatically zero-rated because the customer or payment is offshore: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, and the recipient's status and service type matter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and MRN, together with customs confirmation of exit from the EU
Commercial invoice and sales order identifying the goods, buyer, destination, and VAT treatment
Bill of lading, airway bill, carrier receipt, or other reliable transport evidence
Proof of payment or accounting records where relevant; no inward-remittance certificate is generally required under French law
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. The exporter must retain evidence supporting export exemption and input-tax deduction. If export or other exemption conditions are not substantiated, the DGFiP may assess output VAT, interest for late payment, and applicable penalties. Deliberate evasion or fraudulent documentation can trigger aggravated tax penalties and, where statutory elements are met, criminal proceedings. The specific assessment, penalty, and limitation period depend on the facts and applicable provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and Ministere de l'Economie, des Finances et de la Relance (Tresor Public), with DG Tresor serving as the Foreign Exchange Administration authority under EU Capital Movements Directive and French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monetaire et financier)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions within the EU single market framework; no general exchange control restrictions on euro-denominated flows. Profit remittances by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted subject to (i) corporate income tax of 25% on realised profits, (ii) dividend withholding tax at 25% or reduced treaty rate (e.g. 15% under FR-China DTA, 0% if EU parent directive applies), and (iii) the absence of thin capitalisation or anti-abuse recharacterisation under article 212 of the French General Tax Code (CGI). Payment incidental to current transactions is unrestricted; however, the non-resident exporter must obtain a SIREN/SIRET business identification number and a valid bank account in the SEPA zone to receive proceeds via the standard SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT MT103. Any payment from a French bank account requires a purpose code or narrative enabling the French bank to satisfy anti-money laundering Article L561-2 of the Monetary and Financial Code. No administrative authorisation is required for routine trade settlement below EUR 150,000; cross-border flows above EUR 10,000 trigger automatic reporting to DG Tresor for balance-of-payments statistics but do not constitute control or require prior approval unless involving sanctioned jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose export proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios. Export receipts may be freely retained in EUR or a foreign currency account; nevertheless, French resident companies are obliged to declare cross-border payments exceeding EUR 10,000 to the Banque de France via the 'Rapport de Flux' electronic filing for balance-of-payments purposes within 20 business days of the transaction month-end. The SARL may designate an authorised intermediary bank to execute this declaration. No forced conversion to EUR and no deferred receipt period are applied; invoicing is permitted in any commercial currency, but the functional currency of accounts remains EUR for statutory corporate income tax filing.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for day-to-day treasury operations; Medium for principal banking relationship. French Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) may open accounts with EU-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the PSD2 passporting regime, including entities such as Wise Europe SA, Ebury Partners SAS, Qonto SAS (licensed as établissement de paiement), and Revolut Ltd (passported into France). Such accounts are permissible for liquidity management, inbound capital receipt from foreign shareholders, and e-commerce trade settlement. However, EMIs do not possess a full banking licence and therefore cannot provide credit lines, letters of credit, or commercial documentary collections. For the receipt of proceeds from Stripe and Shopify Payments, a SEPA account at an EMI is sufficient, but the treasury blueprint recommends a Tier 1 bank anchor account to manage regulatory risks and to secure future factoring or trade finance facilities. French AML/KYC imposes a full identification of the beneficial owner and the physical address of the registered office; EMIs may accept remote onboarding via video identification, but the bank account name must exactly match the legal entity name of the French SARL.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all directors is mandatory in principle for full-service Tier 1 commercial banks when the opening entity is a French SARL with foreign shareholders and no prior bank reference. Under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Article L561-5-1) and the AMF/ACPR guidelines, the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding more than 25% of share capital or voting rights must be identified; the managing director (Gérant) must appear for the compliance interview, either in person at a French branch or through a supervised remote videoconference using the ACPR-approved solution (e.g., via an accredited third-party provider such as Liminal or Bankin'). Where non-resident directors are involved, a French organisation in absentia may be accepted if the SARL's registered office is physically rented and the original KYC documentation is apostilled and notarised. Remote opening is feasible at neobanks/PSP-licensed entities, but Tier 1 banks will require a physical meeting of the Gérant and a document review by a local legal counsel. The recommended process is to appoint a French resident Gérant or open the account at a branch where a corporate legal representative attends in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delayed FR-SARL registration records due to Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce’s inactivity period; insufficient recent business bank history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised English/French translation of the Kbis extract showing active registration status; provide an original lease agreement for the registered office; present signed Gérant resolution designating signatories; provide prior shareholder funding documentation including board minutes and bank statements of the parent company evidencing source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ownership through an overseas holding entity with Chinese or Singaporean shareholders and lack of transparent corporate chain of title
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an organisational chart in French demonstrating all intermediate legal entities to the ultimate individual shareholder; furnish UBO declaration forms (article L561-7) signed by all direct owners; provide certified copy of articles of association with notarisation/apostille; and a shareholder registry extract from the corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue concentration involving high-volume small-ticket Stripe and Shopify Payments transactions without structured invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply PDF invoices in French or English for each settlement cycle (STRIPE REPORTS and SHOPIFY ORDERS) matched to the VAT compliance system; present VAT registration certificate (VAT number FRXXXXXXXXX) from the French tax administration; and maintain a clean transaction ledger with purpose-coding to demonstrate regulated business activity within ISIC 4791 online retail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittance of material capital contribution by foreign parent without clear legal basis and foreign exchange reporting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a capital increase deed or share subscription agreement registered with the French registry; file the corresponding E-41 reporting or DG Tresor statistical form if contribution exceeds EUR 150,000; provide signed capital contribution certificate and bank credit advice showing the inbound SWIFT MT103 narrative referencing the capital increase; include parent bank KYC introduction letter (banking comfort).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sensitive jurisdiction exposure or the payment processor as an OFAC/UE sanctioned entity under the EU retained sanctions list (Russia/Belarus/Iran concerns)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a compliance certificate and sanctions screening report issued by an independent screening tool (World-Check, LexisNexis); provide operational flow contract with Stripe Inc. and Shopify Inc. evidencing full compliance with EU restrictive measures; and submit a written legal undertaking that the SARL will not route payments from sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Flow-through of buyer refunds/dispute penalties in the 3D-printer product category creating inconsistent accounting for chargebacks under PSD2/RDR
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full chargeback management policy; monthly Payment Service Provider (PSP) reconciliation statements; maintain the merchant-level processor account with proper documentation of 3D printer product descriptions; and a signed declaration that all refunds are issued in the original payment rail and comply with the Distance Selling Directive.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant processing of the initial shareholder capital subscription and top-up working capital contributions to the French SARL should be executed via SWIFT MT103 with mandatory purpose codes. Recommended message narrative: '/REC/CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION SHARE SUBSCRIPTION SARL FRANCE/ISO COV:TDWP'. Use purpose code (i) 'CIRCLE' or the EU Balance of Payments classification under code 'N99' for capital transfers, or (ii) 'S010' when sourced from direct investment. The remitting bank must reference the French corporate identifier Kbis, VAT number FRXXXXXXXXX, and the bank account IBAN of the SARL. For any inbound remittance exceeding EUR 150,000 the French receiving bank will file the balanced-payments declaration (Rapport de Flux) to DG Tresor; the sending entity must transfer only after the notarial deed or board resolution approving the capital increase has been recorded at the Greffe. Where the parent is outside the EU, the inbound capital is exempt from French withholding tax if recorded as share capital in the category of capital increases; verification of anti-money laundering requires an affidavit of source of funds and a copy of the parent's bank debit advice. The clearing rail prioritises the EUR SEPA Express Instant for amounts below EUR 100,000 (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement) or the SWIFT standard for larger wires.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for purchase of 3D printer consumables (resin, filaments, spare parts) should settle through (i) SWIFT MT103 direct credit for commercial invoices above EUR 50,000, (ii) SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Business-to-Business Direct Debit for intra-EU suppliers, and (iii) Commercial Letter of Credit (Sight MT700) for Asia-based manufacturers if payment in advance risk is unacceptable. An ordinary EUR-denominated MT103 from the French SARL's BNP Paribas account to a Chinese supplier via Bank of China is the standard, with the instruction note 'TRADE SETTLEMENT-3D PRINTER CONSUMABLES-PURCHASE INVOICE NO.XXXX-UNRESTRICTED' and the mandatory purpose code 'G000' (general trade). No French exchange control approval is required for imports; however, the importer must keep the commercial invoice, the AWB/bill of lading, and the customs clearance declaration (Import One Stop Shop if applicable for EU B2C flows) for 10 years. For high-value commercial LC, the beneficiary presents documents at the advising bank in the seller's country, which triggers the reimbursement through the SWIFT MT754/MT756 cycle. Recommended clearing terms are 30/70 or 100% documentary against shipment for the first six transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Vanilla Forward Contracts with a French authorised credit institution (term: 1 week to 12 months) under ISDA French Law Master Agreement
EUR/CNY Deliverable Forwards for cross-border import settlements with China-based suppliers
EUR/USD Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) only where a French regulated counterparty is a member of the NDF market (excluded for retail-facing transactions; must have corporate underlying exposure)
Currency Swap (MT320) between EUR and USD for larger treasury balances above EUR 1,000,000 with a Tier 1 French bank
At-the-money EUR/USD FX Options (European style) purchased for hedging a defined e-commerce platform settlement risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) including balance sheet, profit and loss account and annexes, together with the shareholder decision on profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to EUR 1,500 (EUR 4,500 on repeated default); summons by the Public Prosecutor; court-ordered regularization; prolonged non-filing may trigger judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065 and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December, online filing by 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends, within 6 months of the accounting year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of corporate income tax due (or 30% in case of bad faith), late-payment interest at 0.4% per month, and potential unilateral tax assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) – update on share transfer or controller change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual due date; filing required within 30 days of any definitive change (no annual re-filing for unchanged ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted declaration punishable by up to 6 months' imprisonment and EUR 7,500 fine for individual managers or EUR 22,500 fine for the SARL; potential blocking of distributions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for a SARL exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: total balance sheet above EUR 3,200,000, net turnover above EUR 6,400,000, and 50 average employees; other cases may also trigger the obligation, e.g., control of new group structures, subsidiary status, or express shareholder demand representing a specific minority threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of listed groups or unlisted groups opting for consolidation, but the parent's individual annual accounts remain under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not mandate a periodic annual UBO confirmation filing. The register of beneficial owners must be continuously maintained at the registered office. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership triggers a new declaration to the Greffe within 30 days. For corporate formalities, an updated share transfer register (registre de mouvements de titres) and a copy of the transfer deed are retained on site; banks and regulated partners may impose an annual UBO certification under KYC policies, but no separate government re-registration is due.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%. Reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for SARLs whose group turnover is below EUR 10 million; the balance is taxed at 25%. No statutory tax holiday is available. Specific incentives include the Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) total or partial exemption if R&D qualifies, and the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) at 30% for eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million. Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but annual deduction is capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit in excess of EUR 1 million; carryback is available up to EUR 1 million over 3 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (impôt sur les sociétés) filed via impots.gouv.fr – Espace Professionnel; mandatory electronic filing by EDI-TDFC or EFI.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return, supplemented by four equal advance instalments and one final balance settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For any accounting year ending on 31 December, the 2065-SD annual return must be filed no later than the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For an accounting year ending on any other date, the return is due within 3 months of the end of the accounting period. Instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December during the fiscal year; the final balance is due with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C1 — Résultat de l'exercice (revenu net fiscal de base)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SARL's net taxable result for the year before applying the deficit carryforward or reduced-rate allocation. This reconciles accounting profit/loss to fiscal taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL is a French tax resident entity. Report worldwide taxable profit without distinction as to the residence of its shareholders. Non-resident shareholders do not file this box on behalf of the SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C2 — Plus-values / moins-values nettes à long terme
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose net long-term capital gains or losses from the sale of assets such as intangible IP, equity interests or real property used in the 3D-printer retail operation. Long-term gains may benefit from reduced 12.8% or 25% rates when eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders have no direct filing obligation here. If the SARL is liquidated by a non-resident shareholder, the resulting distribution is taxed separately under dividend and DTA rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C3 — Résultat fiscal après déduction du déficit reportable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the final taxable amount after deducting the permitted loss carryforward. Businesses below EUR 10 million group turnover may allocate up to EUR 42,000 to the 15% reduced-rate band and the excess to the 25% band.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced-rate band is available to the SARL itself regardless of foreign ownership; do not allocate profit to foreign shareholders in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box DD1 — Déduction du déficit reporté
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the amount of prior-year tax losses actually deducted in the current year, respecting the EUR 1 million plus 50% annual recapture limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep a detailed statutory loss tracking schedule in French tax format. A non-resident parent cannot consolidate French losses against profits booked in another jurisdiction absent French tax integration rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box EE — Réductions et crédits d'impôt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible credits such as the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche, family tax credit, or patronage deductions that can reduce the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL may claim credits only for activities carried on in France. Foreign parent entities cannot transfer their credits into the French return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% increase in tax due if the return is filed after formal notice, 40% if more than 30 days late, and 80% for fraudulent concealment. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month on unpaid amounts. Failure to file electronically may trigger a EUR 15,000 penalty and potential automatic onerous assessment. The French tax authority may also impose an automatic minimum assessment for failure to submit balance-sheet schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2572-SD (acomptes et solde de l'impôt sur les sociétés) filed through impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance payments plus annual final settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Advance instalments for the current fiscal year are due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December. The final settlement of the balance is due at the time of the annual 2065-SD return: second working day after 1 May for 31 December year-ends, otherwise 3 months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box AC — Acompte d'impôt sur les sociétés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute each quarterly advance at 25% of the previous year's net corporate income tax, with any required correction for the reduced-rate band and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL must make instalments out of French taxable income. Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to dictate or receive instalment amounts; all payments to shareholders are distributions governed by dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the annual tax actually due on the 2065-SD return against advances already paid. Any balance is payable by the filing deadline. Overpayment may be refunded or carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claims for DTA relief on distributions are not processed through this box. Such claims are independent and follow the withheld-dividend refund procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of instalments results in late-payment interest of 0.20% per month plus a 5% penalty if no notice has been issued, 10% if paid within 30 days of formal notice, and 40% if more than 30 days after formal notice. Fraudulent non-payment triggers 80% penalty. Directors are jointly liable for tax and penalties only where they have intentionally hidden assets or engaged in tax fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: French domestic law applies a 25% withholding tax to dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder and 30% for a non-resident individual, unless reduced or eliminated by an applicable double tax treaty. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive the French withholding tax is eliminated where the parent holds directly at least 10% of the SARL's capital and has held that interest for 24 months. The standard rate may be increased to 75% where the shareholder is established in a non-cooperative jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a certificate of tax residence (TRC/certificat de résidence) from the foreign tax authority and submit the official French Form 5000 to the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP). EU shareholders claiming the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption use Form 5001 with evidence of qualifying holding and holding period. The forms and TRC should be delivered to the French paying company or the DGFiP Centre des Non-Résidents before distribution to trigger the reduced rate at source. If withholding is applied at the statutory rate, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the DGFiP before the expiry of the applicable prescription period, generally by 31 December of the second year following the year in which the tax was paid. In an audit context, the beneficial-owner condition is strictly examined; a mere conduit shareholder cannot obtain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a French SARL to a non-resident are subject to domestic withholding at 30% under Article 119 bis of the French Tax Code, reduced to treaty rates commonly 0%, 5% or 10% for EU and treaty partners. Interest on arm's-length debt paid to a non-resident creditor is generally not subject to French withholding tax, other than a 75% levy on interest paid to non-cooperative jurisdictions; certain participating loans or profit-related interest may be recharacterised as dividends and subject to 25-30% withholding. The SARL must document the beneficial ownership, economic substance and arm's-length character of all cross-border interest and royalty payments to prevent reclassification, denial of DTA relief and application of abuse-of-law penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million annual turnover or balance-sheet assets threshold. A French SARL is required to prepare the full Local File and Master File where the SARL or the parent group exceeds EUR 400 million in turnover or assets, or where the SARL is controlled, directly or indirectly, by a non-resident enterprise exceeding that threshold. Even below the threshold, the SARL must maintain transfer-pricing evidence in its accounting records sufficient to refute a DGFiP recharacterisation of cross-border transactions under Article 57 CGI.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code comparable to UAE or Caribbean regimes. Equivalent substance requirements arise from the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD), the OECD BEPS Action 6 treaty anti-abuse rules, the French abuse-of-law doctrine under Article L64 LPF, and Article 155-A CGI anti-avoidance provisions. The SARL must demonstrate genuine commercial activity, physical or e-commerce operational presence, actual decision-making in France, adequate employees and commercial risk-bearing. A French SARL used as a pure conduit that invoices foreign sales, retains no operational substance, and remits profits to an artificial offshore parent will be treated as a shell, the DTA benefit will be denied, and the managing director may be personally liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Concealment of Turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting online retail sales from 3D printers and consumables by excluding Stripe/Shopify settlement data, recording fictitious supplier invoices, or shifting sales channels outside the French accounting books. Also includes issuing false invoices to non-resident buyers or failing to declare Bank of France balance-of-payment statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 80% of the evaded tax for fraudulent manoeuvres, plus 0.20% monthly late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI is punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 500,000, increased to 7 years and EUR 2,000,000 where committed as an organised gang. Tax authorities may seize bank accounts and assets via conservatory attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant (managing director) and any de facto manager who knowingly signs false returns can be criminally prosecuted, barred from managing a commercial company for up to 10 years, and ordered to pay fines personally. Where the SARL is insolvent and mismanagement caused the inability to settle tax debts, the commercial court may order the director to contribute to the company's liabilities under the action en comblement de passif.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SARL with no real commercial premises, employees or economic function solely to receive payments from 3D-printer sales and channel profits to a non-resident shareholder via dividends, management fees or transfer prices, while the shareholder in fact manages all business activity outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGFiP may invoke the abuse-of-law procedure (Article L64 LPF), disregard the SARL's corporate separateness, recharacterise the profits as belonging to the ultimate non-resident beneficiary, and assess additional corporate tax, 25-30% withholding tax, 80% fraud penalty where bad faith is proved, and late-payment interest. The court may also refuse treaty or Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and shareholders participating in the artificial arrangement may be held jointly and severally liable for the tax and penalties. Directors can face criminal conviction for laundering the proceeds of tax evasion; personal asset confiscation and travel bans may be imposed pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling 3D printers, filaments or resins to a foreign related party at below arm's-length prices, buying components from a related party at inflated prices, or paying non-resident related parties for non-existent management fees, technical services or IP licences. Also includes failure to produce Local File/Master File documentation within 30 days of a formal DGFiP request where the EUR 400 million threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 57 CGI the DGFiP can reassess profits by reference to the arm's-length standard and impose a 40% penalty for intentional breach or 80% for abusive manoeuvres, plus monthly late-payment interest. Failure to produce transfer-pricing documentation may result in a specific fine and adverse evidentiary presumption, shifting the burden of proof to the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign statements containing artificial transfer prices may be personally assessed for penalties and interest if they acted as de facto managers. In a criminal tax-fraud case, the court may prohibit the director from exercising commercial functions and order confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Consciously accepting large cash payments above EUR 1,000 for 3D printers without complying with anti-money-laundering controls, failing to identify the beneficial owner of the payment source, structuring settlements through Stripe/Shopify to avoid disclosure thresholds, or failing to file a suspicious transaction report with Tracfin where unusual indicators are present.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering (Article 324-1 Code pénal) is punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 375,000; habitual laundering carries 10 years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine. The court may also order temporary closure of the business and forfeiture of seized assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is criminally liable if the SARL is used as a vehicle for laundering proceeds of tax fraud. A director who fails to prevent or knowingly facilitates such activity may be sentenced personally, removed from corporate management, and made liable for asset restitution. Even at a Low_Risk_Standard AML tier, proper customer due diligence and transparent payment-rail records are mandatory.
